entities.name: PMID:25093847
observations: In isolated pressurized rat gracilis arterioles, 10–100 µM H₂O₂ caused concentration-dependent constriction; endothelial removal and PLA, PLC, PKC, Src, TXA₂-receptor, or COX inhibition reduced or reversed responses. COX-1 inhibition had a stronger effect than COX-2 inhibition.
Study concludes endothelial Src/PLC/PKC/PLA signaling activates COX-1-dependent TXA₂ synthesis/release, increasing vascular smooth-muscle Ca²⁺ sensitivity.

entities.name: Hydrogen peroxide
observations: H₂O₂ (10–100 µM) elicited concentration-dependent constriction in isolated, pressurized rat gracilis skeletal-muscle arterioles.

entities.name: Arachidonic acid pathway
observations: In rat gracilis arterioles, H₂O₂-induced constriction was attributed to endothelial PLA signaling and COX-1-dependent TXA₂ production/release.

entities.name: Thromboxane A2
observations: TXA₂-receptor blockade converted H₂O₂-induced constriction to dilation in isolated rat gracilis arterioles, supporting TXA₂ mediation.
